findings.reason: the registry name is the section's whole subject; the author must either spell the derived repository as the existing `imas-alambic-jt60sa` (state the slug→repo rule that drops the hyphen) or migrate the deployed artifact to a new name, and the done-when must pin the repository it asserts against so the wrong-name push cannot pass.
findings.text: §18 reads and writes the registry at `ghcr.io/simon-mcintosh/imas-alambic-<machine>`, which for the machine slug `jt-60sa` (§17 fixes `maps/jt-60sa/`) resolves to `imas-alambic-jt-60sa` (hyphen between `jt` and `60sa`), but the existing and facility-deployed artifact lives at `ghcr.io/simon-mcintosh/imas-alambic-jt60sa` (no hyphen): `packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh:44` sets `BUNDLE_REF=...imas-alambic-jt60sa:2026.10.07`, the bundle published in run `r-20261007T034932763033-jtfm-maps-to-ghcr` is named `imas-alambic-jt60sa` with `gh api /user/packages/container/imas-alambic-jt60sa` proving the container package under that exact name, and the migration clause "the current content, GHCR 2026.10.07 and deployed at the facility, is released as v1.0.0" can only be true in that repository. As written, §18's first `maps release jt-60sa --bump major --final` would create and publish to a second, empty registry repository (`imas-alambic-jt-60sa`) while the deployed `imas-alambic-jt60sa` keeps serving `2026.10.07`, so the "one owner" the section sets out to establish is split across two names and the v1.0.0 migration never reaches the artifact actually installed.

findings.reason: the section must add the destination argument (and the version read the installer currently performs) to `pull`, or state how the installer obtains the bundle without it; either way the interface it specifies today does not perform the migration the section rests on.
findings.text: §18 declares `pull <machine> [--version]` with a single fixed destination, "into `maps/<machine>/` for a fresh clone", and states that `install/imasdb.sh` "calls `imas-ambix maps pull` into its staging directory". The command as specified has no `-o`/`--dest` (or output-path) argument, so it cannot deliver a tree into the installer's `mktemp` staging directory (`packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh:66-71`, `BUNDLE=$WORK/bundle`), which is precisely the `oras pull … -o "$BUNDLE"` invocation the section says it retires. The claimed substitution — and with it the "one owner" for the registry, auth form and artifact type — is unreachable through the interface the section names, and a `maps pull` that writes only to the gitignored `maps/<machine>/` would additionally pollute the development tree during every install. The pulled tree's version check (`BUNDLE_VERSION` read from `bundle.json`, imasdb.sh:73-78) is likewise not covered by the specified command.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one new module, `imas_ambix/maps_cli.py`, hides the two-state semver machine, the OCI push/pull over oras, the tree-digest comparison and the tag-state read behind three commands (`release`/`pull`/`status`); the interface is materially smaller than the behaviour it carries.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 names a second GHCR repository, `ghcr.io/simon-mcintosh/imas-alambic-<machine>`, beside the deployed owner `ghcr.io/simon-mcintosh/imas-alambic-jt60sa` at `packages/imas-alambic/install/imasdb.sh:44`, so the release would push to a different repository than the one the plan says it is migrating.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — with public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0, §18 is the one section adding a CLI group, and its "Accounting for the new surface" paragraph names what it retires (the installer's private `oras pull`, merged into `maps pull`) and states why `release` and `status` have no existing command to retire; it therefore meets the rule requiring a section that adds surface to name its retirement or the reason none can be. (The `pull` interface gap below is a design defect, not an unaccounted-for addition.)
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §17 extends the engine's existing bundle discovery (`discover_bundles`, `packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/machine_map.py:234`, whose entry-point loop it broadens to an iterable target) rather than adding a parallel discovery path, and §18 names the prior art it follows — imas-codex's release CLI (`imas_codex/cli/release.py:153`, `imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py:719), and the already-published artifact type `application/vnd.imas-alambic.bundle.v1`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `maps pull` is specified with no destination argument, so the installer substitution §18 claims it performs cannot be done through the interface the section names.
